sections.title: The KRFC Program Guide
sections.content:
The memo presents a daily program schedule for KRFC AM 1313 Internet Talk Radio. It introduces the station as serving the San Francisco Bay Area and says listeners elsewhere can access program transcripts or listen through the listed network methods.

The schedule includes news, interviews, call-in programs, and commentary about networking.
sections.plainLanguage: The document is formatted as a radio program guide. Its programs are built around Internet topics and people.

sections.title: Shows About Networking
sections.content:
The program entries pair real networking subjects with comic premises. They include discussion of Doppler correction for a computer receiver on the Concorde, OSPF testing on 1822 networks, and a show called The Protocol Police that debugs TCP/IP implementations from a hot tub.

Other entries mention port assignments, RFCs, ATM, NFS, and a fictional prize for decrypting a DES message.
sections.plainLanguage: The schedule turns protocol testing, network news, and security into exaggerated radio entertainment. The titles and descriptions make the joke by combining technical subjects with implausible scenes.

sections.title: Purpose of the Memo
sections.content: RFC 1313 is an informational program schedule. It includes news and talk programs about networking. It does not specify an Internet standard.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo presents a fictional broadcast schedule, not a networking specification.
